subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should this stale exec-approvals write class be fixed now through a shared guarded persistence helper, or folded into the broader open node writeback security PR?
rationale: The bug is source-proven and affects command-approval policy, but the permanent fix shape crosses gateway, node, and security-sensitive persistence paths where closed direct PRs and an open broader PR already exist.

options.title: Adopt a shared guarded write fix
options.body: Implement or sponsor a maintainer-reviewed helper that reloads and merges allow-always and usage writes under a lock/CAS contract across gateway and node paths.

options.title: Fold into the broader open PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78226 as the canonical path only after it is rebased, proven, and expanded or confirmed to cover this concurrent allow-always loss case.

options.title: Defer to runtime-state separation
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader runtime metadata split in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67154, accepting that the direct data-loss bug remains open meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Adopt a shared guarded write fix
recommendation.body: Implement or sponsor a maintainer-reviewed helper that reloads and merges allow-always and usage writes under a lock/CAS contract across gateway and node paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest observed path history across the affected exec approval files and is the best available owner for a security-sensitive persistence direction call.
